_what: The squad's render-path bodies - VESPER / KOA / SABLE / SYN on their own D1-minted generated bodies. Room verbs (idle + kneel) landed 2026-08-09; the COMBAT roster (run / aim / fire / hurt / death) and SYN entire landed 2026-08-10, so the yard can stage every fighter on the render body and the door's last visible body swap retires. The reproducible INPUT; the sheets it produces are build output under assets/original/squad_render/.
_decided: 2026-08-09 - the squad phase (idle + kneel, three fighters), decided by the designer from a four-body lineup against the render cipher. 2026-08-10 - the squad-combat phase: run/aim/fire/hurt/death for the three squadmates plus SYN entire (idle/kneel included - his first render verbs; he never idles in the room), generated on the doctrines the cipher roster paid for. The yard flip this feeds is the phase the yard-body PR's corrected seam note named as 'a real generation phase, the designer's call' - and the designer called it.
_economics: The combat phase spent ~266 generations against the doctrine kit's predictions: run rode the running-8-frames template (~1/dir), hurt/death/fire rode v3 (~1/dir + re-roll rungs), and the aim states were the planned 20-40-per-fighter cost. SYN was the expensive citizen again - six states total (aim x4, kneel x2) because the state tool kept regressing his stocky build and red accents to its priors; the roster record predicted him ('he is the fighter who proved compose was Cipher-shaped').
_dialect: left/right ship from south-west/south-east (3/4), matching every roster body. Idle is the breathing-idle template at 4 frames; kneel and AIM are held poses: the still + the compression breath at 2 frames. Fire is 5 frames stage-mapped to burst-first decay (the scalpel cuts time); hurt is a 4-frame flinch; death is a 9-frame one-shot the yard holds flat. Cadences are the room's render96 map, pinned in the yard as RENDER_FPS.
_cdn: frames live at {cdn_root}/{character_id}/... - animations at {source_character_id}/animations/{anim_dir}/{pl_facing}/{i}.png, state stills at {state_id}/rotations/{pl_facing}.png. Idle/run/hurt/death ride the identity character; AIM is its own state; FIRE's animations ride the AIM state (keep_first_frame makes the aim still frame 0, so the shot begins and ends in the stance that hosts it - cipher's seam-by-construction, inherited).

breath._why: held poses (kneel frame 2, aim frame 2): the upper 40% of body rows settles one pixel - compression, not translation. The same dialect and amplitude as cipher's kneel and the pack's.

anchor._why: the RE-FRAME anchors each STRIP by its own measured ground row: dy = FEET_Y minus the strip's max last-opaque row, one constant per strip, never per frame. Constant-within-strip preserves authored sway; per-strip constants put every knee, boot, footfall, and fallen body on the pack's line. The combat phase leans on this harder than the room did: syn's run sank a constant 1-3 rows per strip and the anchor absorbs it; death's deepest row is the lying body, which is exactly what belongs on the line.

mark_guard._why: per frame, the count of pixels within euclidean tol of the fighter's mark RGB must sit within slack of the same count on that facing's identity rotation. The guard's honest scope: gross identity loss and large inventions, NOT subtle defects; the designer's eyeball is the real identity gate. The combat phase re-ratified slack 16 over cipher's absolute +5: cipher's kit carries 4-8 mark pixels, koa's carries 20-25, so a proportionless +5 flunked koa's own headband riding a flinch (worst measured combat excursion: koa hurt SW frame 0 at +8).
mark_guard._aim_scope: the AIM verb baselines its guard on the aim still itself, not the identity rotation: the pistol's mark-colored glow strip is AUTHORED addition (koa's left aim measures +17 mint over his unarmed identity, one past slack), so aim's guard only holds the breath frame to the still. The still's own deviation from the identity was judged at state acceptance, where the lineup eyeball rules.

hurt_checks._why: cipher's hurt contract: every frame's last opaque row within row_tol of the facing's standing row, and the final frame's bbox height >= the identity's minus 1 (the flinch must stand back up - sable's north v2 died here at -4, a pop the room would show at the idle hand-off). The dark budget is the mark_guard above, not a separate constant. Residual, recorded: syn's hurt ends +1..+2 ABOVE identity height on some facings (over-recovery); the recovery clause is a floor and the designer's 1x eye judges the excess.

death_checks._why: cipher's death contract unchanged: the yard holds the last frame, so the last two frames' bbox heights <= 0.68 x the identity's (measured squad finals 12-19 against 33-36 standing - far under), and the final row sits within -1..+2 of the standing line. Deliberately NO last-two-frames identity check (the settle-into-the-floor is the impact reading). Dark budget = mark_guard. The white-flash class the budget CANNOT see (koa's death north v1 flashed the whole body white for one frame - white is far from every mark) is an eyeball gate, recorded here so the next molder knows the metric's blind spot.

fire_checks._metric: TWO-TIER decay, executed against all sixteen keepers before recording: cipher's spatial mask (bright outside the 2px-dilated frame-0 baseline) wherever the flash leaves the silhouette, and bright-CHANGED (bright pixels differing from frame 0) only where it does not - syn's head-on chest flash is the one facing the spatial mask cannot see at all. Bright-changed ALONE was the first cut and it failed its own execution: it conflates flash with recoil, and vesper's south map shipped two flash-free frames in recoil order (7 then 12) that the metric misread as a decay break. Decay claim on the chosen series: shipped f1 >= f2 >= f3 with f1 > 0 and f3 < f1; shipped f4 must be byte-identical to frame 0 (every stage map ends on source 0).
fire_checks.containment: mode radius per facing, scoped to FLASH-COLORED pixels only: outside-baseline bright pixels that are either low-chroma (max-min <= 16 - the white-hot cores) or within mark_guard.tol of the fighter's mark (the tinted fringes). Bright KIT riding authored recoil is not an invention: syn's pale-wrapped fist drops six rows through his south shot and lands 18+ from any honest muzzle point - a radius that included it would gate nothing. The face-star, lime star, ember-feet, and akimbo classes all remain in scope: their pixels are flash-colored and far from the declared point.
fire_checks._color_doctrine: the model's muzzle-flash prior is WARM YELLOW and it invents debris (shell casings, embers, splatters, off-arm poses). Cipher never fought this - his palette ramp is cyan/white, and the prior obliged. The squad's fire prompts NAME the ramp ('white-hot with a <mark> tint - never yellow, orange...'), the per-facing-family position, and the inventions ('no shell casings... the other arm stays relaxed and empty'). Eighth, ninth, and tenth guard-clause saves. SYN's warm flash is the one deliberate exception: dull-red/rust IS his palette's own ramp, recorded below.
fire_checks._dilate_why: 5px, MEASURED like cipher measured his 2: the squad's recoils carry bright kit (koa's white wraps, syn's lit lenses, sable's ember dots) 3-5px off the still's bright zones, and a 2px baseline let them masquerade as bloom up to 36px from the muzzle. The dilation sweep (3/4/5) was executed against all sixteen keepers; 5 is the smallest value that absorbs every kit stray it can, and the color scope below handles the one it cannot.
